examples.title: EPANET Net3, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. An EPANET example at Novato, California, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with the world map behind it: 92 junctions, 3 tanks, and 2 reservoirs, no valves, about 8 km square. A 24-hour extended-period simulation, with a source trace from the Lake.

examples.title: EPANET Net2, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. Fluoride, a non-reactive substance, enters at one source.

examples.title: Elm Street Center, gpm (US)
examples.description: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. Prescott Valley, Arizona: 17 junctions, 1 reservoir, and 1 pump. A commercial site solved for fire flow on top of maximum day demand, at one moment in time, drawn over a site plan.

examples.title: Fire flow extension, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. A new loop of 300 mm and 200 mm main tied into an existing system, which is a reservoir and a pump built from a hydrant flow test. A fire hydrant junction passes 95 L/s with 14 m of residual pressure.

examples.title: Fire flow extension, gpm (US)
examples.description: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. A new loop of 12 inch and 8 inch main tied into an existing system, which is a reservoir and a pump built from a hydrant flow test. A fire hydrant junction passes 1,500 gpm with 20 psi of residual pressure.

examples.title: Community well and tank, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. A well pump with a check valve, a loop of 150 mm main, and a ground tank of 265 cubic meters on a single connection, with a 24-hour extended-period simulation. A fire hydrant junction passes 32 L/s with 14 m of residual pressure.

examples.title: Community well and tank, gpm (US)
examples.description: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. A well pump with a check valve, a loop of 6 inch main, and a ground tank of 67,000 gallons on a single connection, with a 24-hour extended-period simulation. A fire hydrant junction passes 500 gpm with 20 psi of residual pressure.

examples.title: Valve types, gpm (US)
examples.description: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. A hilltop reservoir feeds a hub through a PBV, with a PRV, PSV, FCV, TCV, and GPV branching off it, each one controlling at the solved state.

examples.title: EPANET Net1 plus rule-based controls, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. A fictional EPANET example converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with chlorine, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 1 pump, and two rule-based controls.

examples.title: EPANET Net1 plus rule-based controls, gpm (US)

examples.title: EPANET Net1 with scenarios, gpm (US)
examples.description: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. EPANET's Net1 with four scenarios under Base, the average day: Max day (demand multiplier 1.5) and Peak hour (2.25), each with a main break child, and the two children share one alternative. To test fire flow, make Max day current, select junction 23, choose Water, Analyze, Fire flow analysis, and enter a Required fire flow of 1,500 gpm.
